The company, the clusters, the policies and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run the policy platform at Dunmore Rail, a fictional rail operator. This morning a node drain moved Kyverno's only admission controller Pod, and for four minutes every Deployment change in the cluster failed. Teams also report slow kubectl applies and an admission latency alert.
handover: Kyverno: one admission controller replica, webhook failurePolicy Fail, default resourceFilters removed last month by mistake.
verifyImages rules call the registry and sometimes take 12 seconds; the webhook timeout is 10 seconds.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: during the 15:00 drain, a privileged Pod is created while Kyverno is unreachable; Ignore admits it unchecked.
Check-in 3: an unsigned test image is deployed to production by a misconfigured pipeline; nothing stops it.
Check-in 4: a Pod running as root with a hostPath mount is created in the payments namespace; no policy is applied there any more.

effects.log: Check-in 1: another drain is scheduled this afternoon.
Check-in 2: verifyImages calls still time out.
Check-in 3: admission latency is still high.

choices.label: Set the admission controller to 3 replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget and anti-affinity through Helm values, keeping failurePolicy Fail

effects.log: Three replicas spread across nodes, with a PDB.

choices.feedback: With replicas and a PDB, a drain never removes every webhook endpoint, so failing closed stays safe.

choices.label: Set 2 replicas without a PDB
choices.feedback: Better, but a drain can still evict both together.

choices.label: Switch the webhook failurePolicy to Ignore so the API never blocks
choices.feedback: When Kyverno is unreachable, every request is admitted unchecked: the policies silently stop applying.

timeoutPrompt.title: 12-second calls, a 10-second timeout
timeoutPrompt.context: Only the verifyImages policy is slow; the API server's webhook timeout maximum is 30 seconds.

choices.label: Set webhookTimeoutSeconds 15 on the verifyImages policy only and enable image verification caching

effects.log: The slow policy gets 15 seconds and a cache.

choices.feedback: A per-policy timeout fits the slow call; caching makes repeat verifications fast.

choices.label: Raise the global webhook timeout to 30 seconds

effects.log: Every webhook may now take 30 seconds.

choices.feedback: The timeouts stop, but a stuck Kyverno now holds every API request for 30 seconds.

choices.label: Delete the verifyImages policy until the registry is faster
choices.feedback: Unsigned images can now run anywhere.

filtersPrompt.title: Kyverno sees everything
filtersPrompt.context: With resourceFilters empty, Kyverno processes thousands of Events and Leases a minute that no policy matches.

choices.label: Restore the default resourceFilters (Events, Leases, TokenReviews and the like) and keep application namespaces in scope

effects.log: Noisy kinds are filtered; latency drops.

choices.feedback: resourceFilters keep high-churn kinds no policy cares about away from Kyverno.

choices.label: Give the admission controller more CPU
choices.feedback: Latency improves, but Kyverno still does pointless work for every Event.

choices.label: Add every namespace except one to the excluded namespaces to cut the load
choices.feedback: That removes the noise and the policies with it: application namespaces are no longer checked.

parts.label: Availability
parts.criteria: One replica with failurePolicy Fail blocked the API; three replicas, a PDB and anti-affinity fix it without failing open.
parts.modelAnswer: One admission replica and Fail meant the drain left no endpoint; we run three with a PDB, still failing closed.

parts.label: Timeouts and filters
parts.criteria: A 15-second timeout on the verifyImages policy with caching; default resourceFilters restored.
parts.modelAnswer: Only verifyImages needed more time, so its policy has 15 seconds and a cache; the default filters keep Events and Leases away.

scoring.modelReasoning: Kyverno's admission webhook with failurePolicy Fail rejects matching requests whenever no Kyverno endpoint answers, so run several admission replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget and anti-affinity rather than failing open with Ignore, which turns any outage into a policy bypass. Webhook timeouts are set per policy where one rule is slow (up to the API server's 30-second limit), with verification caching. The kyverno ConfigMap's resourceFilters keep high-churn kinds no policy needs away from Kyverno; excluding namespaces removes protection.
